findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed soda nozzle in front self-service area or be soiled with debris. PIC was informed and nozzle was cleaned and sanitized. Ensure soda nozzles are cleaned frequently to avoid accumulation of debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
findings.comment: Observed time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods stored ambient on prep table with no proper marking for time as a control. The PIC stated that the employee forgot to label the items with the time control stickers. The tomato and lettuce that were unmarked were discarded. The rest of the produce was properly and clearly marked. Ensure staff are using the time as a control stickers at all times and discarding after 4 hours.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.19(C)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (C) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 6 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate: (a) The time when the FOOD is removed from 5C (41F) or less cold holding temperature control, and (b) The time that is 6 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from cold holding temperature control.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed bins holding clean equipment and utensils to be soiled with food and debris. PIC was informed and bin was moved to the dish area. Ensure staff are cleaning the bins frequently to avoid accumulation of food debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed several food employees put on new gloves without washing hands in between glove changes. Discussed proper glove use and hand washing technique with PIC and employees during inspection. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed baffle of ice machine to be soiled with debris. Clean and sanitize baffle of ice machine. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Observed containers used to store clean utensils and cookware to be soiled with food debris. Clean and sanitize containers used to store utensils and cookware. 

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.comment:
6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

Observed an employee beverage and container of half-eaten food on top of a prep cooler, next to dispenser of ice tea. Ensure staff eat in a location away from food preparation or storage areas. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1)  (P) Jr. meat patties are 128°F. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135°F, or above. Reviewed hot holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was discarded. 10 patties were discarded. Patties in the holding container ranged from 147°F to 128°F depending on where they were in the container. Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11  (C) Single-service articles are not protected from contamination at coffee maker. Observed coffee filters to be sitting on top of machine uncovered and unprotected. Single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food and lip contact surfaces are protected from contamination. Coffee filters were moved to their proper place. Reference 4-904.11.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment: 6-305.11  (C) Employee clothing and personal items were found stored improperly. Food establishments shall A) Provide designated dressing rooms or dressing areas for employees that routinely change their clothes in the establishment; B) Provide lockers or other suitable facilities for the orderly storage of employees' clothing and other possessions. Reference 6-305.11. Observed employee jacket hanging on a shelf holding single use items. Jacket was moved to proper storage location.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.11  (C) Grease was found dripping from the components of the exhaust ventilation hood system. Exhaust ventilation hood systems in food preparation and warewashing areas including components such as hoods, fans, guards, and ducting shall be designed to prevent grease or condensation from draining or dripping onto food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles. Reference 4-204.11. Hood vents were cleaned on month ago. Suggest discussing with hood cleaning company what they consider their responsibility to clean and what is the responsibility of the failcity to maintain clean.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text:
750.690 - A) Cover was missing from the front of the microwave under the door, and a heavy accumulation of food debris and general buildup were observed under the microwave. Thoroughly clean under the microwave and provide a durable, cleanable cover to eliminate buildup of debris under the microwave.

B) Flashing of metal pillar behind the microwave was loose along the bottom where the pillar meets the counter directly behind the microwave. A heavy accumulation of food debris and general buildup were observed in the area behind the metal flashing. Thoroughly clean behind the loose flashing and then repair the area with a durable, cleanable seal to eliminate buildup of debris.

Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - Sanitizer concentration at 3 part sink was 0ppm quat. Wall mounted chemical dispenser has been connected backwards, and the sanitizer tube needed to be switched to the wash (detergent) connection in order to dispense at proper concentration. Once the sanitizer tube was attached at the wash connection the sanitizer was observed at proper concentration. All of the dishes from the previous day were to be re-washed and sanitized due to uncertainty of proper ware washing the previous operating day.
The wall mounted chemical dispenser needs to be repaired (see #29 for details).

Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-buckets tested at 0ppm quat. Sanitizer was not dispensing properly (see #29 for details). Buckets were re-made to be at proper concentration of 200ppm 

Maintain quat solutions at 150-400ppm. Use test strips to verify solution is dispensing properly. (see general comments)

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) reach-in freezer used for storage of chicken nuggets and onion rings (food crumbs in the bottom of the unit and along the gasket);   and
B) lower compartment of ICEE machine used for storage of syrup (heavy splash buildup).

Clean the aforementioned items and all non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.
NOTE: ICEE machine might get replaced. Until that occurs, the machine and all general surfaces must be maintained in a clean and sanitary manner.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - Wall mounted chemical dispenser at the 3 part sink is connected backwards. In order for sanitizer to dispense at proper concentration the tubing has to be attached to the wash connection. Upon arrival of inspector, all sani-buckets and the sanitizer at the 3 part sink were observed at 0ppm quat. The detergent and sanitizer tubing were attached at what would normally be their proper connections, but since everything is backwards the sanitizer was not dispensing properly. Manager switched the sanitizer to the wash connection, and the quat solution then dispensed at proper concentration. Manager stated a call for service was made a few weeks ago. Another call for service was made during the inspection. 

Manager stated the technician should be out by tomorrow to make repairs. This issue needs to be resolved immediately to allow for proper dispensing of chemicals without switching of tubing between connections. Until the tubing is adjusted and all repairs are made, management must post signage with detailed instructions on what needs to be done for filling buckets and ware washing process to ensure all employees are following proper protocol for this temporary fix until the dispenser is hooked up properly.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

B) under/behind ice cream and coffee station between the drive thru window and front counter (puddling water and debris).

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.153 - Pans of sliced tomatoes at room temperature on the make line had labels indicating a discard time of 3-4p. Labels were changed to indicate proper 4hr discard time of 1p.

When using time as a control, food shall be marked to indicate the time when products were removed from a temperature controlled environment. All foods must be used or discarded within 4hrs. Properly label time controlled food.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Employee was observed washing hands without use of proper technique. Proper technique was discussed with employee and management. Managers were encouraged to reiterate proper technique with all employees.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment. Proper technique requires the use of soap (wet hands, apply soap, rub vigorously for 20sec), running water, and paper towels to dry hands. After hands have been dried then use the paper towels as a barrier to turn off the manual faucet at the handsink to avoid potential recontamination of freshly washed hands.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text:
750.690 - A) Backsplash at Hi-C machine at drive thru is loose and held in place with tape. Get the machine properly repaired to eliminate the need for tape to hold the backsplash in place or change out the machine.

B) Gasket to reach-in freezer (across from fryers) was torn and soiled with buildup of food debris. Replace the damaged/soiled gasket.

Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

B) Floors were observed to be soiled with food debris and/or grease in the following areas:

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1210 (R) A) Wall was missing tiles by back drive through window. Replace missing tiles. 
Also, caulk the juncture between the wall and the outside of the walkin units.

B) Rough wood was observed above the customer area soda machines. Wood was observed to be splintered/pulling apart in some areas. Employees fill ice in the machines.
Provide proper repairs and seal the wood above the customer soda machines.

Walls and ceilings must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
findings.citation_text:
750.1240 - (R) Light shield was missing above soda syrup boxes. Provide one large shield, individual shields with end caps, or shatter proof bulbs to correct the violation.

All lights in the food prep, food storage or kitchen area of a establishment must be properly shielded (i.e. either have a physical shield or be a shatter resistant bulb) so as to reduce the potential for cross contamination in case of breakage.  Provide properly shielded lights.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.citation_text:
750.1310 - A) Spray bottles of degreaser were hanging on shelving above a box of medium fry pods in the dry storage area. Spray bottles were moved to proper chemical storage area. 

B) Sanitizer bucket in lobby cabinet was observed on top of a box containing child bibs. The box and bibs had moisture on them from the bucket. Staff noted the bibs are a discontinued item. Box of bibs were discarded.

All toxic items must be properly stored separate from food and all food related items (i.e. clean equipment, single service items) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.citation_text:
750.540 - Proof of manager certification was not available for any of the employees currently employed at the facility. A manager came in during the inspection and contacted IDPH to verify the i.d. number and expiration date for her current FSSMC (see general comments for details).

All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.
